claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
The post at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ describes the engine mechanics behind SST's migration from CDK to Pulumi.
AWS CDK allows developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine, which deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and will be released as SST v3 once stable.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
Nitric and Defang also run application deployments through the Pulumi engine.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, supporting AWS and more than 150 other providers.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications...'
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says that on sst deploy resources call an embedded Pulumi engine which calls the bridged Terraform provider, making AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for providers and deployment engine, and Terraform providers are bridged through Pulumi.
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka wrote that the imports from Pulumi mean the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi.
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
Pulumi's engine handles dependency resolution, preview and diff, state tracking, and plumbing to hundreds of provider APIs.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
Any Pulumi user can consume Terraform providers directly via the provider bridge.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed in the same SST app.
SST's latest release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for Sept 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst, formerly sst/sst.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components offer cross-team visibility, central guardrails, and shared infrastructure patterns.
